patterns: Monday questions: James Clear's one-line 'what would the best version of yourself do today?' is the only watchlist post past 5k (~27.6k, 500 likes). Short second-person questions keep winning.
Reading slump is everywhere among small accounts, almost always as a request for the one book that will fix it.
Morning pages and one handwritten page before the phone are circulating again, including people admitting they fell off.
Fountain Pen Day afterglow: ink swatches, gifted pens, handwriting reveals. Small accounts get real replies on these.
Building in public is being questioned out loud: is it worth it, will someone copy me. Those posts draw more replies than the brag posts.
Mental health posts that land name one specific hard part, like asking for body doubling or explaining depression with no obvious cause.

reply_ideas.description: a network security leader saying she's been slacking on her morning pages, quoting a post about writing one page by hand before you touch your phone
reply_ideas.reply_text: I write by hand every morning, and when I slip it's usually because the page started to feel like something I could fail at. Are you going back to full morning pages, or starting with the one page that post suggests?

reply_ideas.description: a graphic design history account sharing a 1962 TOPIC magazine cover by Tom Wolsey, with the line 'The banning, marching, sitting people'
reply_ideas.reply_text: The banning, marching, sitting people is such a good cover line. It makes the protest sound like an everyday habit rather than a headline. Do you know if Wolsey had a hand in the wording, or was he setting what the editors gave him?

reply_ideas.description: an indie hacker asking whether building in public is still worth it if someone can copy your idea and outmarket you
reply_ideas.reply_text: I'm building my brand in public right now, and what I keep noticing is that someone could copy the product but not the reasons I'm making it. Has anyone actually lifted an idea of yours, or is it mostly the worry talking?

bip_draft:
Calmly Crashing is still under construction. The first thing going in the shop is The Smaller Start Kit, printable pages for the days when everything feels like too much, and I'm building it where people can watch.

#buildinpublic
video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on cream paper, a hand writes 'what can I still do today?' at the top of a page with a fountain pen, then one short line under it. Pen and paper sounds only. Post it with the tired-version post.

x_posts.title: Reading slump
x_posts.text:
My feed is full of people stuck in a reading slump this week, and almost everyone is asking for the one book that will fix it. I wonder if the fix is less about the book and more about permission to read something small and not finish it.

What got you out of your last one?
x_posts.why: wave of small accounts asking for the book that will end their reading slump

x_posts.title: Starting again
x_posts.text:
I keep seeing people post that they fell off their morning pages and want to start again. I write by hand every day, and I think the hardest part of starting again is believing the first page has to be worth something.

If you journal, do you write before or after you look at your phone?
x_posts.why: morning pages comeback posts and the one-page-before-your-phone idea

virals_narrative: Slow watchlist day. Only James Clear passed 5k since the last run, with a one-line Monday question about what the best version of yourself would do today (~27.6k). Pinar's small watercolor is outperforming for her size, and Awais Aftab posted on mental health care needing relational care more than new diagnostic language. Outside the watchlist, small readers are stuck in reading slumps and asking for rescue books, people are restarting morning pages, Fountain Pen Day posts are still coming in, and indie builders are openly asking whether building in public is worth the copycat risk. Today's replies and posts come from those threads.
